severe pruritus at these sites that would wake him up at night
denied any recent trauma or history of similar lesions

concepts.why: The patient presents with discrete, dark red, circular lesions in his right axilla, severe pruritus, and no improvement with treatment, which are characteristic of contact dermatitis.

The patient's symptoms of discrete, dark red, circular lesions and severe pruritus are consistent with atopic dermatitis, although the lack of other skin lesions and no history of similar lesions make it less likely.

The patient's physical examination reveals well-circumscribed, violaceous, annular patches, and biopsy findings show lymphocytes obscuring the dermal-epidermal junction, which are characteristic of lichen planus.

The patient's symptoms of discrete, dark red, circular lesions and severe pruritus are consistent with dyshidrotic eczema, although the lack of other characteristic features such as blisters makes it less likely.
The patient's symptoms of violaceous, annular patches are consistent with seborrheic dermatitis, although the lack of other characteristic features such as scale or erosion makes it less likely.

The patient's symptoms of discrete, dark red, circular lesions and severe pruritus, and the fact that treatment with discontinuation of underarm deodorant yielded no improvement, suggest an allergic reaction to deodorant.

rationales.F09: The lack of response to treatment with over-the-counter hydrocortisone cream, ketoconazole cream, and discontinuation of underarm deodorant suggests that the condition may not be contact dermatitis or allergic contact dermatitis to deodorant.
